name: Wave Execution Timeline Template
description: Sprint-level execution timeline template for a single wave of a multi-country CRM migration rollout. Includes parallel workstreams, governance milestones, and three size variants (standard, compact, complex). Based on enterprise pharma best practices for large-scale platform migrations.

phases.name: Requirements & Scope
phases.description: Finalize requirements from discovery phase, lock scope, and establish Change Control Board governance for all downstream changes.
activities: Requirements finalization and sign-off with business stakeholders
Scope alignment for post-discovery build items
Scope Lock milestone — no new requirements accepted after this point
Establish Change Control Board (CCB) — only CCB-approved swaps permitted post-lock
Story cleanup and backlog grooming for build sprints
key_artifacts: CCB charter and swap request template

phases.name: Build & Configuration
phases.description: Parallel build tracks covering standard platform configuration, exception handling, custom solutions, and data migration preparation.

sub_tracks.name: Design of Exceptions (DOE) Build & Test
sub_tracks.description: Build and unit-test exception scenarios identified during discovery — deviations from standard platform behavior that require custom logic.

sub_tracks.name: Module Enhancement / Fast Follow Build & Test
sub_tracks.description: Platform module configuration and enhancement work. Includes standard module setup plus any fast-follow items from prior waves.

sub_tracks.name: Exceptions Build & Test
sub_tracks.description: Build and test exception scenarios that were identified but deferred from DOE. May run later in the build cycle.

sub_tracks.name: Custom Solution Build & Test
sub_tracks.description: Custom development for requirements that cannot be met with standard platform configuration. Includes custom Apex, LWC, integrations, or middleware.

sub_tracks.name: Additional Data & ADTT Build & Test
sub_tracks.description: Data migration development, ETL job configuration, data transformation testing (ADTT), and validation rule setup for migrated data.

sub_tracks.name: Hardening Sprint
sub_tracks.description: Final stabilization sprint before BAT entry. Fix outstanding defects from build-phase testing, optimize performance, address technical debt.

phases.name: End-to-End Testing
phases.description: Full system integration testing in two cycles. E2E validates all modules, integrations, data flows, and cross-functional scenarios together.

sub_phases.name: Pre-E2E Readiness Check
sub_phases.description: Verify environment readiness, test data availability, integration endpoint connectivity, and user provisioning before E2E begins.

sub_phases.name: E2E Cycle 1
sub_phases.description: First full end-to-end testing cycle. Execute all test scenarios across modules. Defects logged and triaged daily. Critical defects block Cycle 2 entry.
exit_criteria: All P1 defects resolved or mitigated
Core business flows pass without critical errors

sub_phases.name: Preview Sandbox Checkpoint
sub_phases.description: Validate build in preview sandbox environment to catch environment-specific issues before Cycle 2.

sub_phases.name: E2E Cycle 2
sub_phases.description: Second full end-to-end testing cycle. Focus on regression testing, defect verification, and edge cases. Typically shorter as major issues resolved in Cycle 1.
exit_criteria: All P1 and P2 defects resolved

phases.name: Platform Release Integration
phases.description: Align custom code and configurations with the platform vendor's release cycle. Validate that new platform releases do not break custom code or configured workflows.
activities: PO Validation — validate upcoming platform release in sandbox environment
Platform sprint alignment — adapt custom code to new release APIs and behaviors
E2E cycle on release build — re-run critical paths on the new platform version
BAT/Preview on release build — verify business acceptance on the release candidate
Release deploy to production
phases.gotcha: Platform releases can break custom code. Always allocate 2-3 sprints for release validation. Never assume backward compatibility for custom Apex, LWC, or integration code.

phases.name: Business Acceptance Testing
phases.description: Business stakeholder validation of the solution. BAT is the final quality gate before production deployment. Business users execute real-world scenarios to confirm the system meets their requirements.

sub_phases.name: BAT Preparation
sub_phases.description: Prepare BAT environment, test scripts, test data, and user accounts. Train BAT testers on the system and test execution process.

sub_phases.name: BAT Kickoff
sub_phases.description: Formal kickoff meeting with business stakeholders. Review scope, test plan, defect process, and go/no-go criteria.

sub_phases.name: BAT Cycle 1
sub_phases.description: First BAT cycle. Business users execute test scripts across all in-scope scenarios. Daily defect triage with SI team.

sub_phases.name: BAT Cycle 2
sub_phases.description: Second BAT cycle. Focus on defect verification, regression, and any scenarios blocked in Cycle 1. Often includes edge cases and negative testing.

sub_phases.name: BAT Close
sub_phases.description: Formal BAT closure. Review defect statistics, confirm go/no-go criteria met, obtain business sign-off.

sub_phases.name: Defect Resolution
sub_phases.description: Fix remaining defects from BAT. Verify fixes in BAT environment. Final regression pass.

phases.name: Training
phases.description: Two-tier training model: Train the Trainer (TTT) first, then end user training delivered by trained trainers.

sub_phases.name: Train the Trainer
sub_phases.description: Train designated super-users and local champions who will deliver end user training. Covers system functionality, common workflows, troubleshooting, and training delivery techniques.

sub_phases.name: End User Training
sub_phases.description: Role-based training delivered by trained trainers. Typically runs in parallel with deploy preparation. Includes hands-on exercises in training sandbox.

phases.name: Deploy & Go-Live
phases.description: Production deployment and staged go-live. Technical go-live (system available) precedes end user go-live (users enabled) to allow internal validation.

sub_phases.name: Deploy to Production
sub_phases.description: Execute production deployment runbook. Validate data migration, integrations, and system health in production.

sub_phases.name: Technical Go-Live
sub_phases.description: System is live in production. Internal validation by SI team and IT administrators. Users are not yet enabled.

sub_phases.name: End User Go-Live
sub_phases.description: Users are enabled in production. Hypercare support activated. Escalation paths communicated to all users.

phases.name: Hypercare & Stabilization
phases.description: Elevated support period immediately following go-live. Dedicated support team monitors system health, triages issues, and provides rapid resolution.
activities: Daily system health monitoring and performance checks
Dedicated L2/L3 support desk with rapid SLAs
Daily defect triage calls with SI team
Sync monitoring and mobile performance tracking
Transition plan from hypercare to steady-state support

phases.name: Next Wave Discovery (Parallel)
phases.description: Discovery and requirements gathering for the next wave runs concurrently with current wave execution to maintain program momentum.
activities: Stakeholder workshops for next-wave countries
Regulatory and compliance requirements gathering
Gap analysis for country-specific requirements
Lessons learned integration from current wave
Sprint cadence for next-wave requirements elaboration
phases.parallel_start: Starts approximately 8 weeks into current wave execution

milestones.name: Requirements Finalized
milestones.description: All business requirements documented, reviewed, and signed off by business stakeholders.

milestones.name: Scope Lock
milestones.description: No new requirements accepted. Only CCB-approved swaps permitted. Critical governance milestone — late scope changes are the #1 cause of wave delays.

milestones.name: E2E Cycle 1 Cutoff
milestones.description: All P1 defects resolved. Core business flows pass. Integration touchpoints validated.

milestones.name: E2E Cycle 2 Cutoff
milestones.description: All P1/P2 defects resolved. Regression suite at 95%+. Performance benchmarks met.

milestones.name: BAT Kickoff
milestones.description: BAT environment ready. Test scripts prepared. BAT testers trained. Entry criteria met.

milestones.name: BAT Close / Business Sign-Off
milestones.description: Business stakeholders confirm the system meets their requirements and approve go-live.

milestones.name: Go/No-Go Decision
milestones.description: Final go/no-go decision based on BAT results, defect status, training completion, and deployment readiness.

milestones.name: Technical Go-Live
milestones.description: System deployed to production and validated by technical team before user enablement.

milestones.name: End User Go-Live
milestones.description: Users enabled in production. Hypercare support activated.

sprint_model.numbering: Sequential within wave (Sprint 1, Sprint 2, ... Sprint N)

defect_management.triage_cadence: Daily during E2E and BAT phases

priority_levels.description: Major — workaround exists and is acceptable

variants.name: Compact Wave
variants.scope: 1-5 countries, typically a single market or small cluster
variants.notes: Compressed timeline for smaller rollouts. Single E2E cycle. BAT compressed to one cycle. Training and deploy overlap. Suitable for markets with minimal customization or where a template from a prior wave is reused.

REQ.notes: Compressed requirements — leverage prior wave templates

variants.name: Complex Wave
variants.scope: 15+ countries across multiple sub-regions, often with sub-waves for staged go-live
variants.notes: Extended timeline for large, complex waves. Countries are grouped into sub-waves (e.g., Sub-Wave 1A in April, 1B in July, 1C in September) to manage risk. Each sub-wave has its own BAT and go-live, but build and E2E are shared. Requires additional hardening sprints and a third E2E cycle.

sub_wave_model.description: Countries grouped into 2-3 sub-waves within the wave. Sub-wave grouping based on: regulatory similarity, language clusters, shared integration patterns, and go-live readiness.

sub_wave_example.scope: 5-10 countries — highest complexity or latest readiness

REQ.notes: Extended requirements phase — multiple stakeholder groups across sub-regions

BUILD-DOE.notes: DOE build — larger exception set across countries

BUILD-EXC.notes: Exceptions build for late-added country requirements

BUILD-DATA.notes: Data migration across multiple source systems per country

BUILD-HARDEN-1.notes: First hardening sprint — stabilize for E2E Cycle 1

BUILD-HARDEN-2.notes: Second hardening sprint — stabilize for BAT entry

BAT-1B.notes: BAT for sub-wave 1B countries (overlaps with 1A deploy)

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Requirements still pending at scope lock
risks_and_mitigations.description: Business stakeholders have not finalized requirements by the Scope Lock milestone, creating pressure to extend scope lock or accept incomplete requirements.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Delays cascade through build, E2E, and BAT. Late requirements may require rework of already-built features.
mitigation: Set hard scope lock date at program kickoff — non-negotiable calendar milestone
Run weekly requirements readiness reviews starting 4 weeks before scope lock
Implement a 'requirements at risk' tracker — flag pending items 3 weeks before lock
For items still pending at lock: defer to next wave or treat as CCB swap requests
Communicate clearly: requirements accepted after scope lock cost 3-5x more to implement

risks_and_mitigations.risk: E2E cycles overlapping with active build
risks_and_mitigations.description: Build work is still in progress when E2E testing begins, leading to incomplete features, unstable environments, and test failures caused by incomplete code rather than actual defects.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: E2E testers waste effort on known-incomplete features. Defect triage becomes difficult — is it a real defect or just unfinished code?
mitigation: Enforce code freeze for E2E scope before each E2E cycle starts
Use feature flags to isolate incomplete features from E2E test paths
Run pre-E2E readiness check — verify all E2E-scope features have passed unit and integration tests
Accept that some build tracks (e.g., custom solutions) may continue during E2E — but keep them on separate branches
Clearly label E2E scope vs. in-progress scope in the test environment

risks_and_mitigations.description: Business users discover during BAT that the implemented solution does not match their expectations, even though it matches the signed-off requirements. This creates pressure to change scope during BAT.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: BAT timeline extends. Go-live date at risk. Team morale drops as late changes create rework.
mitigation: Conduct early showcase demos during build phase — show, don't tell
Include business users in E2E testing — don't let BAT be their first time seeing the system
Classify BAT defects rigorously: is this a defect (doesn't match requirements), an enhancement (new requirement), or a usability issue?
Enhancements discovered in BAT go to post-go-live backlog — BAT is for defects only
Pre-agree on BAT exit criteria with business stakeholders before BAT begins

risks_and_mitigations.description: A platform vendor release introduces breaking changes to APIs, behaviors, or metadata that custom Apex, LWC, integrations, or configurations depend on.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Custom code fails in updated environment. Emergency fixes needed. BAT results invalidated if release hits during BAT.
mitigation: Subscribe to platform release notes and preview programs — know what's changing before it ships
Allocate 2-3 dedicated sprints for release validation in every wave plan
Run automated regression suite against preview sandbox as soon as release is available
Maintain a custom code inventory — know every custom class, trigger, component, and integration
Plan wave timelines around known platform release dates — avoid going live within 2 weeks of a major release
Keep custom code minimal — every custom line is a line you must maintain through every release

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Training compressed due to upstream delays
risks_and_mitigations.description: Build or testing delays push training into the deploy window, leaving insufficient time for effective training delivery.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Poorly trained users on Day 1 leads to high support ticket volume, low adoption, and user frustration.
mitigation: Decouple training content creation from system readiness — write training materials based on requirements, not the live system
Start Train-the-Trainer early — trainers can practice on sandbox even if production isn't ready
Have a fallback training plan: if classroom training is compressed, deploy bite-sized video modules for Day 1 basics
Never sacrifice training for timeline — an untrained user base is worse than a 2-week delay
Build training sandbox early and keep it updated — don't wait for production deployment

risks_and_mitigations.description: In complex waves with multiple sub-waves, a delay in sub-wave 1A (pilot countries) cascades to 1B and 1C because later sub-waves depend on pilot lessons, shared configurations, and the same SI team.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Entire wave timeline extends. SI team capacity becomes the bottleneck.
mitigation: Build buffer between sub-waves — minimum 6 weeks between sub-wave go-lives
Identify and resolve pilot-country issues before committing to sub-wave 1B dates
Run sub-wave 1B BAT preparation in parallel with sub-wave 1A defect resolution
Ensure sub-wave configurations are independently deployable — 1A issues should not block 1B
Staff sub-wave teams with some overlap but not total dependency on the same people

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Data migration quality issues surfacing late
risks_and_mitigations.description: Data migration defects — orphaned records, incorrect mappings, missing audit trails — are not discovered until E2E or BAT because data validation was insufficient during build.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: E2E and BAT blocked by data issues. Users lose confidence in the system. Regulatory risk for compliance-sensitive data (samples, consent).
mitigation: Run data validation rules after every migration load — do not wait for E2E
Implement the Lumis data migration validation checklist (val-dm-001 through val-dm-007) during build phase
Conduct a mock migration (dry run) 4 weeks before E2E — full volume, full validation
Include data quality checks in E2E entry criteria — E2E cannot start until data passes validation
For compliance data (consent, samples), validate with compliance team separately before BAT

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Mobile sync performance not validated until late
risks_and_mitigations.description: Mobile sync performance is acceptable in small test environments but degrades at production data volumes. This is not discovered until late E2E or BAT when realistic data volumes are loaded.
risks_and_mitigations.impact: Go-live at risk. Users cannot work offline effectively. Emergency performance tuning under time pressure.
mitigation: Test sync performance with production-scale data volumes in E2E Cycle 1 — do not wait for Cycle 2
Establish sync time benchmarks early: initial sync < X minutes, delta sync < Y seconds
Profile sync by data volume per user — identify accounts/visits/samples that push the limit
Have a tuning playbook ready: filter configurations, data scoping rules, and sync frequency adjustments
Test on actual mobile devices on actual networks — emulator performance is not representative

use_compact_when: Fewer than 5 countries in the wave
Countries share the same language and regulatory framework
Template from a prior wave can be reused with minimal customization
No complex integrations — standard MDM feed and basic middleware
use_standard_when: Moderate customization — some country-specific exceptions but mostly standard
Single go-live date for all countries in the wave
Established SI team with prior wave experience
use_complex_when: 15+ countries or multiple sub-regions with different regulatory environments
Significant country-specific customizations (e.g., France, Germany, Japan each require unique config)
Multiple go-live dates needed — risk too high for single big-bang
Multiple source systems being migrated (e.g., some countries on Veeva, others on a homegrown CRM)
Wave spans more than one platform release cycle

source: Lumis Knowledge Base — enterprise pharma wave execution patterns
